classification.difficultyReason: Combine surface-area and perimeter constraints, optimise the resulting volume function and recover the base dimensions.

content.prompt:
A closed rectangular box has length $x$ cm, width $y$ cm and height $h$ cm.

It is to be made from $300\text{ cm}^2$ of thin sheet metal, and the perimeter of the base is to be $40$ cm.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that the volume of the box is given by $V=150h-20h^2$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}V&=xyh\\P&=2x+2y=40\\x+y&=20\end{align*}$$

The box is closed, so its surface area is
$$\begin{align*}A&=2xy+2xh+2yh\\300&=2xy+2xh+2yh\\150&=xy+xh+yh\\150&=xy+h(x+y)\\150&=xy+20h\\xy&=150-20h.\end{align*}$$

Substitute into $V=xyh$:
$$\begin{align*}V&=(150-20h)h\\V&=150h-20h^2.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence find the dimensions of the box that meets all the requirements and has the maximum possible volume.

answer.short: $15\text{ cm}\times5\text{ cm}\times3.75\text{ cm}$, with height $3.75$ cm.
answer.worked:
Since $x,y>0$ and $x+y=20$, the base area satisfies $0<xy\le100$. Thus
$$\begin{align*}0&<150-20h\le100\\2.5&\le h<7.5.\end{align*}$$

Find the stationary point:
$$\begin{align*}V(h)&=150h-20h^2\\V'(h)&=150-40h\\150-40h&=0\\h&=3.75\\V''(h)&=-40<0.\end{align*}$$

The volume function is concave down throughout the feasible domain, so its global maximum occurs at $h=3.75$ cm.

Recover the base dimensions:
$$\begin{align*}150&=xy+20(3.75)\\150&=xy+75\\xy&=75\\x+y&=20\\y&=20-x.\end{align*}$$

Substitute into $xy=75$:
$$\begin{align*}x(20-x)&=75\\x^2-20x+75&=0\\(x-5)(x-15)&=0\\x&=5\text{ or }15.\end{align*}$$

The corresponding values of $y$ are $15$ or $5$. Therefore the dimensions are $15$ cm by $5$ cm by $3.75$ cm.

Check: the base perimeter is $2(15+5)=40$ cm, and the surface area is $2(15)(5)+2(15)(3.75)+2(5)(3.75)=300\text{ cm}^2$.
